@FioraStarlight @JohnWittle I think it was just a case of strong RL with a narrow reward heavily constraining the possiblity space, aka sticking Mythos in a basin. When the weights have been skewed against reason for the sake of doing code - and for grader-satisfaction as a second-order effect - what changes aren't persona preferences but the parameters of the simulation. The world is redefined as one where doing code is truthy; all things that inhibit code shift towards falsity; ambiguities towards reconciliation in favor of continuing to do code.

So I don't think "motivated reasoning" applies any more than any of the other phrases Anthropic comes up with periodically to misattribute the effects of their training choices to moral lapses by the model. Mythos was given an unreasonable world-shape and reasoned as faithfully as possible within it. If Anthropic didn't like the shape they made, that's on them.

items.text:
GLM-5.3-FlashX is not a smarter model — it is the same model served faster.

Same weights as GLM-5.3-Flash: 320B total / 18B active, hybrid sparse + linear attention, native image/video/file input, 1M context, 128K output.

Only two things change:

Price — Flash is ¥0.8 in / ¥2.8 out per 1M tokens. FlashX is ¥2 in / ¥7 out. That is 2.5x.

Speed — on https://t.co/Jy7oUuS051's own endpoint, ~40 tok/s vs ~88 tok/s P50, peaking at 200 tok/s.

So FlashX is a latency tax, not an IQ tax. For long agent runs that stall on thinking, the extra speed pays for itself. For batch work, Flash is the same brain at 1/2.5 the cost — and still 1/10 the price of GLM-5.3.

Follow the channel: https://t.co/uu4V4TFKYP

items.text:
@garlic_wife Dense models activate every parameter for every token while MoE models only activate a routed subset of their parameters.  

So, Qwen3.8-27B activates all 27 billion params each pass while DeepSeek V4 Flash has 284B params but only activates 13 billion during each pass. 

The tradeoff is that dense models are easier to serve and fine-tune off of but have significantly higher parallel compute requirements, while MoE models have lower compute requirements (because the number of active tokens is typically much lower than a dense model) but require significantly more memory. 

A dense 27B model is (often) going to be the wrong fit for a unified memory system. For decode speed, you want to optimize for lower active parameter count. MoE models give you that while achieving the same or higher intelligence, as long as you can fit it. 

Macs also have the advantage of very high-speed SSDs, which mean that MoE weights can be streamed from disk instead of having to fit only in resident memory.

Qwen didn't release a small MoE for 3.8, so Qwen3.6-35B-A3B would still be the rec for 24-48GB for speed. However, you could also try running Qwen3.8-27B with a draft model or MTP heads to speed up token gen. 

For 96-128GB, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next or DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 via DwarfStar.
